title: Quasi-finite boundary of fibrewise nonempty opens in good curve compactifications
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $I$ be a finite set and, for every $i\in I$, let $t_i:T_i\to B$ be finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], let $b_i:C_i\to T_i$ be smooth and proper [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-proper-morphism], and suppose every fibre $(C_i)_s$ is nonempty, geometrically connected and of dimension at most one [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $u_i:O_i\hookrightarrow C_i$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $(O_i)_s$ is nonempty for every $s\in T_i$. Put $C=\coprod_{i\in I}C_i$ and $O=\coprod_{i\in I}O_i$, regarded as an open subscheme of $C$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and let $Z=(C\setminus O)_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow C$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Then the induced morphism $Z\to B$ is separated, quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Empty $I$, empty $B$ and empty $T_i$ are permitted.

proof.text: Factor the structure map from the coproduct of C_i through the coproduct of T_i. The private proved helper proper_sigmaMap identifies the pullback over each open component T_i with C_i: the images of distinct coprojections are disjoint, and the coprojections cover. Properness is local on the target, so the componentwise proper maps b_i give properness of this coproduct map. The existing proved source-library instance AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.sigmaDesc makes the map from the finite coproduct of T_i to B finite, hence proper. Their composite is proper. Empty families are included.

By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], $Z\to C$ is a closed immersion with underlying image $C\setminus O$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] to the proper morphism $C\to B$ from step 1: $h:Z\to B$ is proper. Hence $h$ is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $B$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] gives local finite presentation of $h$. It is quasi-compact because it is of finite type. Its diagonal is a closed immersion by separatedness, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and therefore of finite type and quasi-compact. Thus $h$ is also quasi-separated, and the finite-presentation convention in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] shows that $h$ is of finite presentation.

For each i and s, the existing smooth-fibre criterion makes the scheme fibre smooth over its residue field. The proved source theorem IsRegular.of_smooth (recorded by lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular) gives regularity over this arbitrary field. Local finite type over the residue field gives local Noetherianity; properness of b_i gives compactness of its fibre and thus Noetherianity. The geometric connectedness hypothesis gives ConnectedSpace. The proved IsRegular.isIntegral (lem-sc-regular-connected-integral) gives integrality, hence irreducibility. No perfectness or algebraic closedness is used.

Take the inverse image of the open range of u_i under the fibre inclusion. It is open by continuity, and a point in the nonempty fibre of O_i supplies a point in it using fiberHomeo. Apply the existing proved topological theorem IsOpen.finite_compl_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one, recorded by lem-sc-nonempty-open-complement-finite-dim-le-one. Its image under the fibre inclusion contains exactly the points of C_i over s outside the range of u_i, so this set is finite.

proof.text: Fix $b\in B$. For each $i$, the finite morphism $t_i$ is quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-finite-qf], so [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] says that $S_{i,b}=t_i^{-1}(\{b\})$ is a finite set. The component description [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and the image statement [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identify the underlying set $h^{-1}(\{b\})$ with the disjoint union, over $i\in I$ and $s\in S_{i,b}$, of the sets $E_{i,s}$ of step 4: a point of $Z$ lies in a unique $C_i$, its image under $b_i$ is a unique $s$, and it is outside $O_i$. Here [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies points of $(C_i)_s$ with points of $C_i$ mapping to $s$; no base-change invariance of the reduced subscheme structure is asserted or needed. There are finitely many indices and each $E_{i,s}$ is finite. Hence $h$ has finite fibres.

The boundary morphism is proper, so it is separated, locally of finite type, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the locally Noetherian base supplies local finite presentation. Each fibre is finite by the previous step. Apply the existing proved Scheme.Hom.discreteTopology_fiber_and_quasiFiniteAt to give the scheme fibre its discrete topology, so every asFiber singleton is open. This is exactly the finite-type and isolated-fibre-point definition of Scheme.Hom.IsQuasiFinite. Assemble the five asserted properties.
